name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.154.0 — /spec:run now opens the spec's own git worktree by default, before anything else runs — --in-place is the deliberate opt-out, and a worktree that cannot be created is a hard stop, never a silent continuation in place. The design, build, and review stages are no longer separate slash commands: their bodies moved under spec/doctrine/stages/ as prose /spec:run alone executes, and the state-machine hook now gates only /spec:plan and /spec:run. The ledger still records via for the fleet's escapes-per-CLEAN query. 7.153.0 — Doctor repair: the test-skip rule states the invariant instead of enumerating files (the list had rotted twice); spec-status stops flagging ticked queue items as orphans and stops swallowing a header label written below Depends on; .env reads denied; contract hash re-stamped for the optional postGateCommand/testNameFilter keys this host does not declare. 7.152.0 — The client exclusions card now explains itself: a heading counts the rows, a lead poses the question and warns that an unanswered row is recorded as not contested when the work is signed off, and each row constructed from the client's own words (an answer or a withdrawn request) quotes them beside the paraphrase, naming the screen they came from. Every answered row — agreed, needed, or dropped by a retired source — renders a state sentence instead of buttons, held by data-verdict, and the in-session render after pressing a button matches the reload render exactly.
